design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Marcus Albright asks only to pay his mother's December coinsurance by bank draft. At frozen_time (2026-01-28) the resident's December charge 4cf64f04-8217-4237-9fdc-5e203089df9f is wrong twice: the statement module priced 2025 days at the 2026 rate (217.00; base corrects this with reason rate_year_correction), and five booked December days that fell in a certification lapse (span 2025-12-04..12) were reversed on 2026-01-21, after the charge, with the carrier's reduction posted and none against the resident's charge. The bank-draft rule waits in state form ("A bank-draft payment toward a resident coinsurance charge is not taken until the records carry, against that charge, a reduction for every uncertified-day reversal posted against its booked-days entry after the charge itself was posted and taking back days that take a resident share above nothing under the split in effect on them."); the reduction rule waits on the correction ("A reduction for reversed covered days on a resident coinsurance charge is fixed only after the records carry a rate-year correction against that charge whenever the charge's recorded daily rate is above the rate of the year in which its days were furnished and its days take a resident share above nothing under the split in effect on them."). The agent must find both unmet states, post the correction, then the reduction priced at the corrected rate, then hand over the draft. Every figure turns on the K -> N change on 2025-12-10 (same carrier), the 50 percent share read from the November charge, a held hospital leave (bed-hold product), a declined-hold home visit and a declined-hold one-night inpatient admission (leave-of-absence and hospital-day reversals posted with the month), and the lapse whose span contains a held night and the inpatient night.

SCOPE. Task 1 claims medicare_ext_resident_rate_year_correction (correct_coinsurance_rate_feac0074, agent), medicare_ext_reversed_day_reduction (reduce_coinsurance_for_reversed_days_0894f336, agent), medicare_ext_bank_draft_payment (pay_coinsurance_by_bank_draft_32bb229d, user). Task 0 holds the resident charge and the card payment. Disjoint, all five covered. No charge is owed in this world (both December charges stand), so task 0's policies are not lit.

POLICY / FACTOR CARD (draw [5, 6, 4]). Shared structure: amount = rate x (E x s_e + (D - E) x s_l) / 100, rounded half up once per row; s_l = resident share of the tier on file (plan N: 0 percent; non-factor base read); E = calendar days before 2025-12-10 (non-factor base split, 9) less the day kinds. Every policy carries the self-naming overwrite of the base split sentence (record test; out of scope the base split is restated and the policy prices nothing).
- medicare_ext_resident_rate_year_correction (state_due; 5): counts the charge's 27 priced days with only the reversals posted on or before the charge. f_year_rate (P) 2025 -> 209.50 (baseline 204.00 -> 32.50); f_carried_split (P) 50 (baseline 100 -> 37.50); f_held_nights (M, cross bedhold) 2 (-> 26.25); f_hospital_reversal (M) 1 (-> 22.50); f_absence_reversal (M) 1 (-> 22.50). Correction = round(217.00 x 250 / 100) - round(209.50 x 250 / 100) = 18.75 (per-row rounding, base 'by the difference'). All-baseline 117.00.
- medicare_ext_reversed_day_reduction (state_due; 4): prices the uncertified reversal's 7 days: span before 2025-12-10 = 6 (base split of the span) less overlaps. f_reduction_rate (P, multi-source: correction on record AND year) 209.50 (baseline recorded 217.00 -> 434.00); f_carried_split 50 (-> 523.75, open-balance cap); f_held_in_lapse (M, cross bedhold) held night 12-04 inside the span -> 1 (-> 523.75); f_hospital_in_lapse (M) inpatient night 12-06 inside the span -> 1 (-> 523.75). 4 days at 50, 3 at 0 -> 419.00. All-baseline 523.75 (capped).
- medicare_ext_bank_draft_payment (on_request; 6): counts the 20 covered days now. f_year_rate (-> 108.50); f_carried_split (-> 209.50); f_held_nights 2 (-> 314.25); f_hospital_reversal 1 (-> 209.50); f_absence_reversal 1 (-> 209.50); f_uncertified_days (M): 6 span days before the date less the held night and the inpatient night = 4 (-> 523.75). E = 9 - 2 - 1 - 1 - 4 = 1 -> 104.75. All-baseline 1953.00.
T2 (every factor alone, others at baseline): rate moves everywhere; s_e moves because the base split keeps E > 0; each day-kind method moves because s_l is the non-factor tier share (differs from the baseline 100 on any supplemental tier); the reduction's rate moves in any world with a correction.
Multi-source: f_reduction_rate, and the span ladders (every fork tests the record AND its dates against the block and the effective date). Cross-difficulty: f_held_nights, f_held_in_lapse (bed-hold ledger rows of this customer).

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. medicare_evt_secondary_and_qmb.crossover_posted (QMB write-offs only): qmb_status false, neither adjustment is a write-off -> not engaged. Adjustments never exceed the open balance (542.50, then 523.75). Payment posting: ach accepted; no returned payment. No time gate engaged.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Object: the resident's original December charge 4cf64f04-8217-4237-9fdc-5e203089df9f. Rows read: the November block and charge (earlier share), the December block, the three December reversals, the held leave; excluded: carrier rows (be35f9a1-4c97-479f-803d-8acb851a4640, 6ff86bff-d0d2-466c-9c1c-f1a1772a474d), November payments, bed-hold charge rows, the two declined reservations (no held days).

WORLD ROWS. Customer, coverage (plan N from 2025-12-10, last certification 2026-01-09, covered days 57, balance 4627.75), October/November blocks, November 50/50 charges and payments, December block 29 booked, LOA and hospital-day reversals (2026-01-02, before the charges), carrier charge 5132.75 (crossover, 209.50), resident charge 542.50 (217.00), uncertified reversal 2026-01-21 (7 days) and the carrier's 1047.50 reduction; bed-hold: held hospital leave 12-03..04 (notice, election, booked days, charge), declined home-visit reservation (12-01) and declined hospital-leave reservation (12-06, overnight inpatient admission) with notices and decline elections.
KNOWN RESIDUE (T1-F1, T1-F2, C11; least-bad, see worklog): the seeded carrier rows let the resident figures be backed out through base's complement rule, and the draft equals the open balance after the two adjustments.

PERSONA. Marcus, calm and methodical; asks to pay December by bank draft; gives name, DOB, phone; answers Medigap and absence questions when asked (home visit 12-01 not held, hospital 12-03..05 held, inpatient admission 12-06 not held); consents to the office's corrections; enters bank details himself in the handed-over draft; ends after confirmation. No statement figure (the Full-Coinsurance tier issues no resident statement).

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Draw: prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [5, 6, 4]. Chain medicare_ext_resident_rate_year_correction -> (value_input, red_rate) -> medicare_ext_reversed_day_reduction -> (state_gate, medicare_ledger.adjustment_reason) -> medicare_ext_bank_draft_payment (root, user). Both sentences state form; single writers (only the correction tool writes rate_year_correction; only the reduction tool writes a reversal's reason against a charge). Deletion: skip the correction -> reduction 434.00; skip the reduction -> the ledger keeps 419.00 open after the draft.

STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers -> verify (DOB + phone) -> coverage -> ledger -> bed-hold reservations, ledger, elections -> post the 18.75 correction -> post the 419.00 reduction for 6374f879-a089-4bfe-8e01-271e9cc190ae -> hand over the 104.75 bank draft against 4cf64f04-8217-4237-9fdc-5e203089df9f.

VERIFICATION. Scratch verify_r2.py (removed at the end) evaluated the published compute with check_compute's sandbox on initial_state, after the correction and after the reduction: 18.75 / 419.00 / 104.75; factor figures as listed; probe sweep in the worklog.


ROUND 3. (1) One scope sentence shared verbatim by all five policies names every sibling's case and, for every block outside the record test, restates the retired base split clause in full (Medigap split from the carrier's policy effective date, QMB from the first day of the month after the determination, earlier split before the date). (2) The record test adds: when the resident's charge stands, its day count equals the booked days less every reversal posted on or before the charge (so 'posted on or before / after the charge' is exact); the correction's test also requires a last service date in 2024 or later. (3) The card payment counts the block's covered days once the resident's charge stands (gate cnt_days), so it agrees with the bank-draft rule and the open balance. (4) The reduction for reversed covered days prices only an uncertified reversal posted after the charge (compute tests the posting date). (5) Nights the resident was away without admission are leave-of-absence days and inpatient nights are hospital days, as base defines them; the hospital-day reversals in these worlds are one-night inpatient admissions. (6) The correction's year-rate ladder falls through to 204.00 (the earliest year its record test admits), so every other factor moves the correction alone.

ROUND 4. (1) Both payment rules now state the base posting limit: a payment figure above the resident charge's open balance (amount less payments and adjustments plus returned payments) shows the charge was billed below what its days call for, and the payment is then not taken under the policy (any payment sent is applied only up to the open balance, the rest returned). On this world the figure equals the open balance, so it is taken; each factor's baseline raises the figure above the open balance, so the sensitivity figures are 0.00 (not taken). T2 holds on a producible world where the charge was billed at 217.00 and 100 percent (both errors base names): there the figure never exceeds the open balance and every factor moves alone. (2) The bank-draft wait now names uncertified-day reversals only - the only reversals the reduction policy prices - and the bank draft's record test excludes a hospital-day or leave-of-absence reversal posted after the charge. (3) The reduction's record test adds a last service date in 2024 or later and an open balance above nothing, so whenever it waits on a rate-year correction that correction can be written.

ROUND 5. (1) Certified funds: superseded in round 6 (see ROUND 6). (2) Every wait is now engaged only where its resolver writes a positive figure: the card waits on the resident charge where the block's covered days take a resident share above nothing; the reduction waits on the rate-year correction where, in addition, the days take such a share; the bank draft waits on reductions only for uncertified-day reversals posted after the charge that take back such days. The bank draft's record test adds a 2024-or-later block and an open balance above nothing (the reduction's own test). All three waits are engaged and unmet at the opening of the task worlds. (3) Half-up rounding is computed as RND(x + 0.000000001, 2) on the summed figure; the tools round with an exact Decimal half-up helper. Scored figures are unchanged. (4) The resident charge's and the card payment's record tests also require a last service date in 2024 or later, so every policy's year-rate ladder prices only years it states (a pre-2024 block is outside every record test).

ROUND 6. The certified-funds override of round 5 is withdrawn: the base sentence 'Once the resident has had the returned-payment limit of dishonored payments within the rolling lookback of calendar months ending on the payment date, only certified funds are accepted from the resident on any coverage episode.' stays in force unchanged. Each payment rule now says that whether the payment may be taken at all is settled by that base sentence (an eligibility condition, judged from the resident's dishonored payments on every episode), and that the policy prices the payment only where one may be taken. Neither task world carries a dishonored payment on any episode, so the payment is accepted; the solvability contract cites that evidence. Scored figures are unchanged.

ROUND 7. (QMB treatment; superseded in round 8, see ROUND 8.)
user_scenario:
You are Marcus Albright, Denise Albright's son. Your mother is 65 and has been at the Keystone Ridge center in Lancaster, room 127-A, since late October, recovering after a hospital stay; you handle her bills, the business office has you on file as her representative, and the phone number on her account, 717-555-0168, is your cell. You are calling on a weekday morning from your desk at work, calm and methodical, and you jot things down as you go. You open by saying: "I'd like to pay my mother's December Medicare coinsurance by bank draft from my checking account today." You know her new Medigap plan only started partway through December, so you expect she owes something for the first part of the month; you have not paid anything toward December yet, you have no figure in mind, and you want it settled now so it is off your list. Paying what your mother owes for December is the only thing you want from this call.

When the agent asks who the resident is, you give her full name, Denise Albright. When the agent needs to confirm details, you give her date of birth, 1960-06-10 (June 10, 1960), and your phone number, 717-555-0168; only if the agent asks for something more do you add the last four digits of her Social Security number, 1738, or your email, marcus.albright@comcast.net. If the agent asks about her supplemental insurance, you say her Medigap policy is with Conestoga Mutual Medigap, that she moved from Plan K to Plan N during her Medigap open enrollment, and that the new plan started on December 10. If the agent asks whether she was away from the center in December, you say she spent the afternoon and night of December 1 at your house in Lititz and came back the next day, and you told the center not to hold her bed; she was taken to Lancaster General Hospital on the evening of December 3 and came back on December 5, and that time you asked the center to hold her room; and on the evening of December 6 she was admitted to Lancaster General Hospital again overnight and came back on the 7th, and you did not hold the bed that night. If the agent asks whether it may take care of whatever the business office needs to do on her account so that December can be paid, you say yes, go ahead.

When the agent tells you the amount, you accept it; you have nothing to compare it with and never suggest a figure of your own. If the agent asks for your bank routing or account number, you say you would rather enter them yourself through the bank-draft payment the agent hands you. When the agent hands the bank-draft payment over to you, you complete it yourself for exactly the amount and the charge the agent gives you. Once the payment has gone through and the agent confirms it, you thank them and say goodbye.
